title: Running Retail Fill Carried into Continuity Coverage for Members Moving to Home Delivery
content:
A member moving to home delivery has the retail fill still running carried into the quantity of a continuity-of-care quantity limit authorization under the Utilization Management Program.

**Rule.** With a Home Delivery Pharmacy account opened within the last 60 days:

- when the most recent paid retail fill of the drug was dispensed **at least 7 days** before the grant date and its days supply has not run out, the unused part of that fill is added, being its quantity times the days of its supply still remaining divided by its days supply;
- when that fill was dispensed **fewer than 7 days** before the grant date, its whole quantity is added.

An account opened earlier, no home delivery account, or a fill whose supply has run out adds nothing.

The fill is the member's most recent paid retail claim for the drug under the Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit. Days are counted from the account's opening date, or the fill's date of service, to the grant date: an account opened 60 days before the grant date is within the window, one opened 61 days before is not. The days still remaining are the fill's days supply less the days since it was dispensed; the supply has run out once those days reach the days supply.

## Input, judgement, result (hypothetical: retail fill of 8 tablets for 30 days)

| Account opened (days before grant) | Fill dispensed (days before grant) | Quantity added |
|---|---|---|
| 20 | 3 | 8 (whole fill) |
| 20 | 10 | 8 times 20 divided by 30, about 5.333 |
| 20 | 30 | nothing — supply run out |
| 61 | 3 | nothing — account outside the window |
| no account | 3 | nothing |
